findings.title: Client removal listener throws UnsupportedOperationException under V2 because guard checks the V1 feature flag
findings.body: In registerListener, the event handling is now guarded by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) (the V1 flag), but the handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 feature is enabled (which depends on the V1 feature being enabled), management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The ClientRemovedEvent listener therefore throws on every client deletion on a server with V2 enabled, breaking client deletion even in realms that do not use fine-grained admin permissions. The guard should also exclude the V2 feature (or the V2 implementation should be a no-op instead of throwing).

findings.title: canExchangeTo/isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions throw UnsupportedOperationException from live request paths
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo (line 149), isPermissionsEnabled (line 189), getPermissions (line 204) and setPermissionsEnabled (line 194) all throw UnsupportedOperationException. These are not dead code: the token exchange flow invokes canExchangeTo on the admin permission evaluator (AdminPermissions.evaluator returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 feature is enabled), and the admin REST 'management/permissions' endpoints for a client invoke isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions/setPermissionsEnabled. With the V2 feature enabled, those requests will fail with a 500 error instead of being denied or handled. These overrides should return a safe default (e.g. false/null) rather than throwing, or the calling code must be updated to handle V2.

findings.title: hasPermission(client, scope) can pass a null Resource to PolicyStore.findByResource and NPE
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no resource exists for the specific client, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). That method returns null when the schema is not supported for this resource server (e.g. realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled() is false while the admin permissions client still exists) or when the aggregate 'Clients' resource was never created (realms whose admin permissions client was initialized before this change, since init() only creates resources on first setup). The null is then passed directly to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource), which throws a NullPointerException (store implementations dereference resource.getId()) instead of cleanly denying access. A null check on the result of getResourceTypeResource is needed before querying the policy store.

findings.title: init() does not migrate existing admin permissions clients: 'Clients' resource and new scopes are never created
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null (lines 226-228), so realms that already enabled admin permissions under V2 before this change (Users resource type only) will never get the new 'Clients' aggregate resource or the new scopes 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope' and 'map-roles-composite'. On such realms, creating a Clients permission referencing those scopes fails ('Scope [configure] does not exist' / 'No scopes found' ModelException from getOrCreateResource line 108), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String scope) at line 244 silently returns false because findByName for 'Clients' yields nothing — admins appear to have no client permissions at all with no diagnostic. A migration step is needed to add the new scopes and the 'Clients' resource to existing admin permissions clients.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission includes the aggregate 'Clients' resource name in the returned client-id set
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). The aggregate 'Clients' resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init() also carries type 'Clients', so it is included in the callback. When a blanket permission on it is granted, the method adds the literal string "Clients" to the returned set of names. Callers that treat the result as the set of client IDs the admin may access get a bogus entry that matches no client, and more importantly a blanket all-clients grant is represented as a single meaningless ID rather than 'all clients', so a filtering caller would show the admin an empty client list despite the grant. The aggregate resource (name equal to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) should be excluded, and a grant on it should be surfaced as a wildcard/all-clients result.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() incorrectly describes them as boolean getters
findings.body: The newly added javadoc on requireView() (lines 95-98) reads "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}" — but requireView() is a void method that throws ForbiddenException based on canView(), not canViewClientScopes(). Likewise the javadoc for requireViewClientScopes() (lines 100-103) says "Returns {@code true} if ..." for a void require-method. The docs contradict the method signatures and reference the wrong predicate.
